plan_90_days: Weeks 1-2 (Oct 26-Nov 6): run the disclosed 2-week test. Output: 3 spec sheets (40/53/67 MVA 138-34.5 kV LTC; 84 MVA 230-34.5 kV; 60 MVA 69-13.8 kV GSU); RFQs to 8 sellers with at least 6 written quotes (weeks, $/MVA, new vs reman, origin, FAT, warranty, storage); 20 buyer calls (8 utility, 6 EPC/IPP, 6 data-center) yielding at least 5 documented 6-month-plus transformer-critical delays and at least 2 written price indications; energy/regulatory counsel engaged (DPA 50 U.S.C. 4512 and EO 14420 provenance memo, at most $25k); listen in on the RPU pre-bid call Nov 5 and submit the Lodi question by Nov 2 on schedule weighting and deferral.

Weeks 3-4 (Nov 9-20): decision gate Fri Nov 13. Output: one-page go/no-go memo tallying the three kill rules; proceed only with at least 3 documented cases, at least 2 written indications, and fewer than 3 of 6 dealers closing the gap.

Weeks 5-8 (Nov 23-Dec 18): secure the supply path and write the term sheet, fee-only, no inventory. Output: 2 signed OEM or OEM-agent letters by Dec 4 stating whether a buyer deposit can be tied to a production slot and whether unit transfer is consented; a one-page date-certain reservation term sheet sent to 5 buyers with at least 2 written indications at 8%+ over benchmark or one paid reservation fee; 1 formal proposal submitted via an OEM teaming agreement on a schedule-scored RFP (Lodi closes Dec 18); cross-fit database v0 with at least 40 surplus/cancelled/in-production units from at least 5 sources.

Output: 1 signed brokered or matched deal of at least 1 unit (at least $1.5M) with fee at least $45k (3%) or a paid reservation fee; qualified pipeline of at least $25M across at least 10 named units with energization dates; vendor registration on at least 3 public-power portals (LP&L Bonfire, publicpurchase.com, NBU); $1.0-1.5M pre-seed with at least $1.0M soft-circled from 3-5 angels/industry operators by Jan 22.
quit_conditions: By Fri 2026-11-13 (test): stop if 3 or more of 6 dealers quote 20 weeks or less at 8% or less over benchmark on at least 2 of 3 specs; or fewer than 5 of 20 buyers name a documented transformer-critical delay of 6 months or more; or no buyer gives a written indication at 8%+ or a reservation fee.

By Fri 2026-12-18 (supply): stop the principal/pooled-deposit model if zero OEMs or OEM agents will state in writing that a buyer deposit can be tied to a production slot and that a unit can be transferred; fee-only brokerage is then a side business, not a company.
By Fri 2027-01-22 (day 90): stop if no executed deal of at least $1.5M or paid reservation fee, or qualified pipeline is under $15M.
By Fri 2027-04-30: stop if cumulative closed revenue is under $6M (about 3 units), or realized gross margin on closed units is under 5%, or cash burn exceeds $400k with under $150k of fees earned.

By Sat 2027-07-31: drop the principal model if no unit has been sourced at 10% or more below replacement cost (no floor tier), since without it contribution is about $0.9M against about $1.6M of opex.
Any time: stop if quoted lead times for new 40-100 MVA units fall under 70 weeks from at least 3 OEMs, or benchmark price falls more than 10% from about $32.5k per MVA.

unit_economics.price: Benchmark $32.5k per MVA (Lubbock April 2025: two 50 MVA for $2,928,000 = $29,280/MVA at 60 weeks; Rystad $30-35k/MVA), so a 60 MVA unit is $1.95M. Sale price by tier: floor (cancelled finished unit) +17.5% = $2.29M; reassigned +10% = $2.145M; reserved +5% = $2.05M (2-3% reservation fee is credited at order, not extra revenue). Observed price of speed in public power is low: Harbor Springs paid +3.4% ($1,323,270 vs $1,279,391) to save about 2-3.5 years.
unit_economics.cac: About $85k per first-time customer (estimate): public-power path about $100k per win (60-100 hours of proposal work at $15-25k per bid, 1-in-5 win rate); private path about $70k (4 industry events $40k plus one BD hire $170k over 9 months, 3 customers). Assumptions, not sourced.
unit_economics.gross_margin: 6-10% blended (refined pitch claimed 11-13%). Tier margins: floor 25% ($0.574M on $2.29M, bought 12% below replacement), reassigned 9.1% ($0.195M), reserved 4.8% ($0.098M). 12-unit year (2 floor, 4 reassigned, 6 reserved): revenue $25.5M, gross profit $2.5M (9.9%), direct costs about $0.78M, contribution about $1.7M (6.8%). Without any floor-tier units: gross 6.2%, contribution about $0.9M.
unit_economics.payback_months: 12-18 months from first contact. A customer taking 2 units a year yields about $290k contribution (about $145k per unit) against $85k CAC, which is about 3.5 months of contribution flow, but cash arrives 9-18 months after first contact. Business break-even is about 11-12 units a year (about $25M revenue) for an 8-person team costing about $1.6M; about 22 units without the floor tier; about 36 units for a 25-person team (about $5M).
unit_economics.capital_to_first_revenue: About $150k to first brokered fee (counsel $40-60k, E&O insurance $25k, travel $30k, entity/registrations $10k, runway); about $1.0-1.5M to first matched-principal sale (bid/performance security, LC support, team cost); the refined pitch's upside needs about $25-30M equity plus a $50-60M warehouse line, which I would not plan for before the supply-side proof exists.
unit_economics.notes: Cost of money: Fed funds 3.75-4.00% after the 2026-09-16 hike, SOFR about 3.87-3.90% in early October, warehouse line assumed at SOFR+400bp = about 7.9%. Direct costs per non-floor unit about $55-58k (LD/warranty reserve 1% $21k, insurance and LC fees $9k, FAT witness $15k, financing carry $10k; transport passed through). If incumbents force the reserved tier to +2.5%, gross profit (about $49k) falls below direct cost, so that tier cannot be the profit center. Fee-only path: assumed 3% agent commission = $64k per $2.145M unit (assumption, 3-5% typical). Private-buyer value of time (assumption): 50 MW at $100-150/kW-month is $5-7.5M a month versus a $2M unit, so critical-path private buyers can rationally pay 15-30%; public power rationally pays 1-4%. $120M upside = about 56 units a year, about 36% of the refined pitch's own $335M reachable-payer estimate. Margin and cost items marked assumption are what the 2-week test and Phase 3 channel letters are designed to measure.

result.biggest_risk: No defensible premium and no guaranteed supply. Buyers who would pay (private owners on a signed-tenant clock) already have direct OEM frames, JCL/Sunbelt stock, Quanta/EPC bundles and temporary units (Lancium/Mortenson used three temporary 345 kV main transformers). Buyers who are plentiful and reachable (public power) buy by RFP at about benchmark and paid only +3.4% at Harbor Springs to save years. On supply, no source shows an OEM will accept a newcomer's pooled-deposit reservation or consent to a unit transfer (Hitachi signs direct end-user frameworks), and cancelled orders may be double-orders that never became built units. Without a floor tier of cancelled units sourced 10%+ below replacement, contribution is about $0.9M against about $1.6M of opex.
result.mitigation: Gate everything on the 2-week test (Nov 13) and a written OEM/agent letter on slot-to-deposit tie and unit-transfer consent (Dec 18); stay fee-only and hold title only against a signed buyer PO and deposit; target private-owner segment (Aligned-type OFE buyers, EPCs like Mortenson) for the premium and use public RFPs only for credibility and market data; build the cancelled-unit database and sell into JCL/Sunbelt as a sourcing partner; plan the exit as acquisition by JCL, Sunbelt/TJC, Quanta or an OEM rather than a stand-alone dealer.
result.founder_fit: Two to three people: (1) a 15-year-plus transformer sales or utility/EPC substation procurement veteran who knows impedance, BIL, vector group and approved-plant lists and has 100+ buyer contacts (ex-OEM sales at Hitachi, Prolec, Hyundai, Virginia Transformer, Siemens Energy, or ex-utility supply chain); (2) a trade-finance/commercial operator who can structure LCs, bid and performance bonds and a warehouse line (ex-JCL, Sunbelt or an equipment lessor); (3) fractional energy-regulatory counsel for DPA, EO 14420 and Build America Buy America. A first-time founder without industry insiders cannot sell $2M sole-source units to utilities; pair with a veteran or spend 12-18 months at a dealer/OEM first.
result.verdict: Thin and crowded. The gap exists only for private buyers with a signed tenant, where a month of delay costs several times a unit's price; public power buys by RFP and paid just 3.4% to save years at Harbor Springs. JCL already sells "reserve capacity now" and Sunbelt Solomon has the capital. Realistic result is a fee-driven boutique, break-even near 12 units a year, not $120M. Start only with an industry co-founder and the two-week test.

result.biggest_risk: You only get the books nobody with a back office wants, and they leave. The Munich Innung listing shows revenue down about 27% in two years; ROM, HomeServe and GREENOX take the better estates within weeks; private maintenance customers can leave on one month's notice (BGB 309 Nr. 9, from the critics' evidence); WEG administrators need about three quotes for larger jobs. Retention under 70% together with utilisation under 65% pushes contribution below 15%, and you learn it around month 12 after the capital is spent. Behind it sits the capital risk: a first-time operator raising no-exit equity for tranches B and C with no LP identified.
result.mitigation: Pay on retained revenue (45% contingent over 24 months, 10-15% escrow); price only B2B repeat revenue with top-10 customers under 40% and exclude consumer and tendered books; require measured technician utilisation of at least 65% from time sheets before bidding; cap each cluster at 3 hubs until the month-12 gate passes; walk away above 0.5x; make HomeServe or ROM the exit for hubs that miss the 15% gate; spend nothing beyond about EUR 40k until the Phase 0 pass test and the dated quit conditions are met; stay at the small median size by design if no anchor LP appears by month 36.
result.founder_fit: Two people who already hold what the pitch lacks. First, a German-speaking Elektro or SHK Meister (or Betriebswirt des Handwerks) who has run a firm of 10+ staff, has an Innung/HWK network, and can be the registered Geschaeftsfuehrer of a hub under Sec. 7 HwO; sellers and administrators will not discuss their crews with anyone else. Second, a deal and paper operator who has closed small asset purchases (law firm, transaction services or search fund), can handle Sec. 613a BGB, earn-outs and escrow, and can build the cash model. A solo founder without German, Handwerk credentials or a Meister partner cannot execute the 90-day plan.
result.verdict: Not attractive to start as specified. Deal flow is real (at least six German SHK or electrical firms entered preliminary insolvency in October 2026 alone), but ROM Technik absorbed a 55-person electrical firm in 46 days, HomeServe (about EUR 100M) already owns the back office, the 19% contribution holds only above roughly 69% technician utilization in a falling market, and no-exit equity is unidentified. Run only a 12-week, under-EUR 40k test, led by a German-speaking Meister.

Alive but unattractive as a Monday start. Its public site shows no AI product and no fixed-price offer, so there is a gap today, but not one that survives a visible customer win. Likely response, fastest first: (1) buy your orphan target first with its add-on mandate, or bid it past the 6.5x EBITDA / 0.9x revenue cap; (2) offer the same bounded scope as an optional fixed price inside the engineer-of-choice contract the owner already has, which is the most damaging move because it needs no new supplier evaluation and ENERCON already holds hours history per deliverable class; (3) poach the scarce independent verifiers; (4) let USA, which reports $72M+ documented value and a 37:1 return and wants "measurable duplications and similarities", write your measured hours benchmark into the next S&L or ENERCON renewal. result.biggest_risk: The edge does not exist, or exists and the buyer takes it. The only thing separating this from the Pelican/Arlington roll-up is that AI plus independent verification cuts total accepted hours by 30% or more on calculation-grade work with 90%+ first-pass acceptance. Evidence is drafting-only: an INL case study estimated ~50% savings on a safety-analysis chapter but found hallucinations and a leak-rate limit of 10,500 cc/s against a 5,500 source value; Westinghouse's 25% is sponsored; nobody has measured calculations or change packages. Even if real, the owner's own review hours do not fall, the discount is under 2% of what the co-op already books per member, and an incumbent can match the narrow scope inside an existing contract. Cap liability at fees (no-charge re-performance plus a fee credit, no consequential or lost-generation exposure, no EPC scope). Get 3 written E&O indications with nuclear and AI disclosed by Jan 15 or fall back to T&M with a not-to-exceed. No auctions and a hard month-12 stop-buying rule. Sell overflow to incumbents as sub-tier rather than requiring displacement.

plan_90_days: Week 1 (26 Oct-1 Nov): sign one insider advisor (ex-AMS delivery head, IT finance or ITAM lead) with 1-2% equity; build a 40-name list from ITAM, IT finance, vendor management and PE portfolio-operations contacts, starting with the ten named buyers; counsel-reviewed NDA. Week 2 (2-8 Nov): send 40 outreach messages offering a free 48-hour 'retirable spend' list; get AP exports, SSO or usage report and application inventory from 3 companies; rank 15+ units of $25k+ each per company with renewal date and named owner. Output: 3 companies sharing data by Day 7 (else run 12-call fallback), 45+ units ranked.

Day 14 (Mon 9 Nov) gate: company contact emails owners 'we plan to retire or downsize on [date] unless you object'; show the CFO or Controller the one-page term sheet. Pass = identified at least 6% of supplied base at 2 of 3 companies, written agreement on at least 50% of dollars with objection no more than 25%, and 2 of 3 finance contacts accept a share of 25% or more.

Day 30 (25 Nov) checkpoint: 3+ NDAs signed, 2+ X-ray proposals out, 1 CFO markup of the term sheet.
Weeks 5-8 (23 Nov-23 Dec): sell paid X-rays into calendar-year budget flush at 8 qualified conversations a week. Day 60 target: 2 paid X-rays signed at $50k or more.

Weeks 9-13 (24 Dec-22 Jan): deliver X-ray 1 in 3-5 weeks (ranked units, clause read, CFO sweep memo, Wave 1 offer limited to units with payback of 18 months or less); start SOC 2 Type I readiness; open 2 specialty-lender conversations. Day 120 (23 Feb 2027) gate: one signed program agreement at 25%+ share on a $40M+ base signed by a CFO or Controller. No engineering is funded for any client before that signature.
quit_conditions: By 2 Nov 2026 (Day 7): fewer than 3 companies agree to share data -> run the 12-call fallback; if median realization of identified dollars on past decommissioning programs is under 30%, stop.
By 9 Nov 2026 (Day 14): identified under 4% of base in 2 of 3 companies, or written owner agreement under 25% of dollars, or finance caps the share at 15% or prefers Redress or in-house -> stop.

Any time: cost to win a signed program agreement above $400k, or median first-meeting-to-signed-X-ray time above 120 days -> stop.

unit_economics.price: Estate X-ray $75-150k fixed (credited against first-year fees if a program is signed within 6 months); then 30% of verified annual invoice reduction for 36 months on units we fund and execute (25% from wave 3 on), 20% on negotiation-only lines, 15% on co-funded units, plus a 10% tail on still-verified reduction for months 37-84. Blended about 26% plus 8% tail. Benchmarks: Redress 25% of savings beyond best-and-final (primary), SaaS-buying services $30-250k plus 15-30% (vendor-authored).
unit_economics.cac: About $0.24M per signed program agreement on a $45M base ($0.15M + 0.2% of base, refined-pitch model). Sanity check: one hunter at about $300k loaded plus advisor fees and travel closing 1.5 program agreements a year on a 9-18 month cycle is $0.2-0.25M each, partly offset by X-ray margin ($100k price less about $55k delivery cost).
unit_economics.gross_margin: Funded model: about 40% gross (revenue $2.6M over 7 years less $1.1M engineering and $0.45M delivery), about 27% contribution after CAC ($0.7M). Lean co-funded variant (15% share, client pays engineering at cost plus 10%): roughly 55-60% on about $1.6M of seven-year revenue.
unit_economics.payback_months: Per unit about 16 months (engineering 0.35 x annual saving divided by a 26% share = 1.35 years). Per client on my ramp math about 50 months (about 4 years) from signing for the funded model, because CAC and engineering are front-loaded and fees ramp from month 9 to about $55k a month by month 36. Lean variant about 12-18 months.
unit_economics.capital_to_first_revenue: About $70-150k to the first paid X-ray (month 2-4) if founders are unpaid; first revenue $50-150k. About $150k net ($450k gross spend against about $300k of X-ray fees) to reach the first success-fee dollar (month 9-15) in the lean variant. The fully funded model needs about $28M peak cash (median case) or $32M (upside) in the model; plan $45-60M.
unit_economics.notes: Reference client: $45M fee-eligible external application run base (assumption; Brunswick's actual base is undisclosed), 6% reduction at year 3 and 7% at year 5 ($3.15M run-rate), 26% share, 8% tail, so about $2.6M of revenue per client over 7 years with $1.1M engineering, $0.45M ops and $0.24M CAC. Austin cross-check: tier A execution-dependent savings of $22-65M a year at 30% would be $6.6-19.5M a year of fees, but the city budgets only $5.8M then $14.2M of savings, a 30% fee on which is $1.7M then $4.3M a year. Unsourced: E&O premiums, SOC 2 cost, lender pricing for contingent receivables (revenue-based financing blogs quote 15-40% APR; performance-based receivables are advanced at 80-90% in one government-contracting source). Sources: Austin memo and committee deck, Rimini Q2 2026 release, Redress pay-from-savings page, refined pitch sections 5.3-5.6.

result.biggest_risk: Owners do not release the money, so funded engineering never converts to a falling invoice line. Evidence: a health-system panel realized about 5-6% of a 20% application-cut target and spent about $1M of labor to save $200K of licences; Austin has verified $8.1M against $49-142M identified (6-17%), budgets $5.8M next year, and says collecting the data took over 4 months. Related blockers: multi-year VMware terms (Metropolitan Council renewed to 2031), acquirers honoring existing contracts, and carriers adding AI exclusions to E&O.
result.mitigation: Fund nothing before a CFO-signed program agreement and written owner sign-off on at least 50% of Wave 1 dollars; start Wave 1 only on lines with invoice end or renewal dates inside 9 months (licence, SaaS, hosting, support) where engineering is near zero; cap funded engineering at about $250k per client until the first audited invoice drop; co-fund (15%) any unit above 0.45 x annual saving; read contract term and minimums in the paid X-ray before proposing a unit; keep work human-led and AI-assisted with the client's own change process and a 60-90 day scream test; kill on the Day-14 and Month-12 gates rather than drift.
result.founder_fit: Needs an enterprise insider (10+ years in IT finance, ITAM or vendor management, or a former AMS delivery head) with a CFO-level network, an engineering lead who has run decommissioning and data-archive work, and someone who can negotiate share-of-savings contracts with a Controller. A young or outside founder cannot get a CFO to hand over AP exports and sign a 3-year fee alone, so the insider co-founder is not optional. M&A integration office or PE portfolio-operations exposure is the fastest way in.
result.verdict: A real wedge with named buyers and a cheap test, but a thin, capital-hungry, services-like business: funded model pays back in about four years per client, and realization evidence runs 6-30%. Run the 14-day test. Proceed only as the lean co-funded variant (paid X-ray, 15% share) with an insider co-founder, expecting a $5-20M firm, not a venture outcome.

result.incumbent_response: Strongest rival: Alsco (fifth-generation family firm, Salt Lake City). It has closed four tuck-ins in about 18 months (Churchill 2024, MacIntosh in PA/NJ 2025, Topper Jun 2025, Advanced Linen Mar 2026), and Advanced Linen's president said he and his partners chose Alsco to care for their customers. Closest copy of the pitch: Wildman Business Group (Warsaw IN, ~500 staff), which keeps plants, names and teams, keeps the owner on managing key accounts, and advertises itself as the alternative succession plan to the nationals. Best-funded new entrant: Unitex with CVC Strategic Opportunities (2026-09-03; family stays in charge, acquisitions named as a use). PE platforms (Falcon, A&M/Atlantic City Linen, Calera/ImageFIRST) already do family rollover routinely, and peer acquirers Dempsey (TRSA board chair), Phelps and Quintex own the owner-to-owner trust channel. Expected response once the platform is visible: Alsco approaches the same owners with a strategic price (7-9x for route-dense books per a buy-side broker, unverified, versus 5.5-6.5x here; each turn is about $3.75M on a $3.75M-EBITDA anchor), leads with trust and track record, and wins wherever it has a plant within about 60 miles. Counter-move: screen out any target with an Alsco/Wildman/Cintas/UniFirst plant within about 60 miles before the first call; never enter a process with two or more strategics; win on what an all-cash buyer cannot give (20-35% pari passu rollover, board seat, formula put after year 4, real estate kept, 120-day close with proof of funds attached to the LOI); use deal 1's owner family as the reference for deal 2; keep Alsco and Wildman as exit buyers rather than enemies. Honest limit: a $5.6M rollover on a $22.5M price is worth about $8-11M later only if the seller believes the thesis, which needs references the platform does not yet have.

unit_economics.price: Buy at 5.5-6.5x normalized three-year EBITDA (~0.85-1.0x revenue), walk away above 7x, with 65-80% cash, 20-35% rollover, holdback up to 1x EBITDA. unit_economics.cac: About $280K out of pocket per closed anchor (QoE on two LOIs $120K, counsel on two LOIs $100K, environmental $30K, travel/events $30K), ~1.2% of EV, excluding founder time. Funnel assumed: 60 listed, 25 conversations, 5 second meetings, 3 IOIs, 1 close.

Platform fee stream is above 80% margin before founder pay.
unit_economics.payback_months: About 16-18 months after the first close on fee income (~$370K year-1 cash fees vs ~$280K deal cost plus ~$300K runway), about 26-30 months from start. The real payback is equity (rollover and carry) at a year 5-7 exit: 5-year anchor model gives 1.5x/8% IRR with platform overhead at a flat 6.0x exit, 1.7x/12% without overhead, 2.3x/18% at a 7.0x exit with margin to 16%, and 1.07x/1% at 7.5x entry.
unit_economics.capital_to_first_revenue: About $350-550K: $120-250K at risk if a deal breaks (QoE $40-90K, counsel, environmental) plus $150-300K founder runway for 9-12 months. First revenue arrives at the anchor close (months 9-12). Sources: Citrin Cooperman 2025 and McGuireWoods 2022 independent-sponsor surveys, CT Acquisitions, Vestis Q3 FY26 release, BD Emerson QoE costs. Full math in the report; model is mine.

result.biggest_risk: Sellers have better, trusted alternatives (Alsco, Wildman, CVC-backed Unitex, PE platforms with routine rollover), so the platform either cannot buy at or below ~6.5x or only gets what strategics decline (adverse selection: deferred capex, key-person risk, no fold-in value). Nobody has found a closed 2025-26 multiple for a sub-$15M independent, and at 7.5x entry my model returns about 1% IRR. Secondary: the capex-stressed targets carry SBA or energy-service liens and cannot change control until plants are commissioned.
result.mitigation: Run the 25-call owner test and 60-day IOI gate before spending anything, with the hard kill rules above. Restrict targets to owners with a capital or transition reason and no strategic plant within ~60 miles. Underwrite at 6.0x with a 7.0x walk-away and a 0.5-1.0x retention holdback. Treat Tier A firms (Arway, Loop, Gunderson) as minority-recap relationships now and control conversations after commissioning (Arway mid-2026, Gunderson May 2027, Loop about Oct 2027). Make the operator co-founder the credibility bridge and let the first acquired family become the reference.
result.founder_fit: A two- or three-person team: (1) an operator who has run a plant or regional P&L at a TRSA-type laundry, is known to family owners, and has a clean non-compete; (2) a deal-and-finance partner with lender and capital-partner relationships and lower-middle-market or independent-sponsor closing experience; (3) counsel on call for environmental, pension and labor diligence. Each founder needs $150-300K of personal runway or a salary elsewhere because fee cash arrives only after the first close. A solo founder, or a team without an operator the owners already trust, loses on the credibility gap alone.
result.verdict: Not attractive to start unless a three-week owner test passes. Alsco, Wildman and CVC-backed Unitex already sell the same family-to-family exit with more cash and a record; my anchor model returns about 8% IRR in the median case and about 1% at 7.5x entry. Price decides everything, no closed sub-$15M multiple exists in the evidence, and none of the ten named targets is for sale. Run only the 25-call test; spend nothing else until it passes.
